# Java Container Images Deep-Dive

This repository contains examples used in the *Java in Containers Deep-Dive*,
which is part of the JVM and Application Performance workshop.

---

### Performance Disclaimer

The performance values shown in this workshop are for reference only and should
not be treated as absolute. Results can vary depending on hardware, system
configuration, runtime environment, and other factors. Readers are encouraged to
conduct their own tests under controlled conditions to obtain accurate
measurements relevant to their specific use case.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) runtime

- [Dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive), or other similar tool, to analyse
  the container image.

- [Oracle Account](https://profile.oracle.com/myprofile/account/create-account.jspx)
  to access [Oracle Container Registry](https://container-registry.oracle.com/)

3. Compare a Java `OutOfMemoryError` with a container killed after exceeding its
   memory limit. Show how to distinguish the failures and what evidence remains
   available for diagnosis.
4. Run a Java container with a read-only filesystem and identify the paths that
   still need to be writable, such as temporary storage, JFR recordings, heap
   dumps, or application caches.

## Common Commands

1. Build all projects

   Please note that some tests require external dependencies that are not
   managed by Maven and will fail if not provided. That’s why these tests are
   skipped in the following example.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package -DskipTests
   ```

2. Run a goal for a specific project

   ```
   ./mvnw <goal> [<goal>*] --projects <project> [<args>*]
   ```

   Example:

   ```shell
   ./mvnw compile --projects 'all-in-one-spring-boot'
   ```

3. Update dependencies and plugins

   ```shell
   mkdir -p './target'
   ./mvnw versions:display-plugin-updates > './target/plugin-updates.txt'
   ./mvnw versions:display-dependency-updates > './target/dependency-updates.txt'
   ```
